stem: When coordinating post-transplant bone-health care, which medication aligns with standard references for treating osteopenia or osteoporosis?

options.text: No pharmacologic therapy is ever used for post-transplant bone disease
Denosumab is permanently contraindicated in all transplant recipients
Only intravenous iron replaces bone-density therapy

explanation.rationale_correct: Treatment of osteopenia or osteoporosis may include denosumab (Prolia), bisphosphonates, calcitonin, hormone replacement in selected patients, calcium and vitamin D, and exercise.

rationale_incorrect.B: Multiple pharmacologic bone therapies are listed when indicated.
rationale_incorrect.C: Denosumab is a listed treatment option rather than being universally contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.D: Denosumab is a bone-directed therapy rather than iron supplementation alone.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → Preserve bone health → Prevent or treat osteopenia/osteoporosis

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → Preserve bone health → 2.d. (denosumab [Prolia]); PDF p. 322 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Denosumab therapy angle distinct from bisphosphonate counseling (cctc-3118) and calcium/vitamin D recall (cctc-3117); anchor verified on Cupples p. 322.

stem: A post-transplant recipient with osteoporosis asks about non-bisphosphonate medication options. Which therapy aligns with standard bone-health references?

options.text: Calcitonin is never used after transplantation
Nasal calcitonin is contraindicated in every recipient regardless of indication

explanation.rationale_correct: Bone-health treatment options include calcitonin (Miacalcin nasal), denosumab, bisphosphonates, hormone replacement in selected patients, and calcium and vitamin D supplementation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Calcitonin is listed among post-transplant bone therapies.
rationale_incorrect.C: Calcitonin is a bone-directed therapy rather than a vaccine.
rationale_incorrect.D: Calcitonin is an option when indicated rather than being universally contraindicated.

stem: During long-term follow-up of a liver transplant recipient on calcineurin inhibitors, the coordinator reviews renal dysfunction risk. Which outcome aligns with standard references?

options.text: Renal dysfunction may progress to renal failure requiring kidney transplantation
Immunosuppression prevents all renal dysfunction after nonrenal transplant
Renal dysfunction never progresses beyond mild laboratory changes
Kidney transplantation is never required for immunosuppression-related renal failure

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term immunosuppression teaching notes that renal dysfunction may develop over time from medications, pre-existing kidney disease, infection, or hypovolemia and may progress to renal failure requiring kidney transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Calcineurin inhibitors and other factors contribute to renal dysfunction rather than preventing it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Renal dysfunction may progress to renal failure in some recipients.
rationale_incorrect.D: Kidney transplantation may be required when renal failure develops.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → j. Long-term effects of immunosuppression → iv. Renal dysfunction
primary_anchor.quote_hint: May progress to renal failure and need for kidney transplantation

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) treatment teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression is a treatment option for PTLD.
Rituximab may be used in PTLD management.
Radiotherapy is never used for PTLD.
Surgery may be used for localized PTLD disease.

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD management includes immunosuppression reduction, rituximab, and surgery for localized disease. Statement III is false because radiotherapy is listed among PTLD treatment options.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—surgery may be used for localized disease.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because radiotherapy is a listed treatment option.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 4. Treatment options
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression … Rituximab … Surgery for localized disease … Radiotherapy

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 4.a., 4.c., 4.f., and 4.h. (IS reduction, rituximab, surgery, radiotherapy); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. PTLD treatment-modality combo distinct from PTLD risk/prevention combo (cctc-3112) and rituximab single-item counseling (cctc-2122); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.
